382: /* SDIO Card Common Control Registers definitions
383:  * see https://www.sdcard.org/developers/overview/sdio/
384:  *                             sdio_spec/Simplified_SDIO_Card_Spec.pdf
385:  */
386: 
387: #define SDIO_CCCR_REV                    0x00 /* CCCR/SDIO Revision        */
388: #define SDIO_CCCR_SD_SPEC_REV            0x01 /* SD Specification Revision */
389: #define SDIO_CCCR_IOEN                   0x02 /* I/O Enable                */
390: #define SDIO_CCCR_IORDY                  0x03 /* I/O Ready                 */
391: #define SDIO_CCCR_INTEN                  0x04 /* Int Enable                */
392: #define SDIO_CCCR_INTPEND                0x05 /* Int Pending               */
393: #define SDIO_CCCR_IOABORT                0x06 /* I/O Abort                 */
394: #define SDIO_CCCR_BUS_IF                 0x07 /* Bus Interface Control     */
395: #define SDIO_CCCR_CARD_CAP               0x08 /* Card Capability          */
396: #define SDIO_CCCR_CCP                    0x09 /* Common CIS Pointer        */
397: #define SDIO_CCCR_BUS_SUSP               0x0C /* Bus Suspend               */
398: #define SDIO_CCCR_FUNCSEL                0x0D /* Function Select           */
399: #define SDIO_CCCR_EXEC_FLAGS             0x0E /* Exec Flags                */
400: #define SDIO_CCCR_RDY_FLAGS              0x0F /* Ready Flags               */
401: #define SDIO_CCCR_FN0_BLKSIZE_0          0x10 /* FN0 Block Size            */
402: #define SDIO_CCCR_FN0_BLKSIZE_1          0x11 /* FN0 Block Size            */
403: #define SDIO_CCCR_POWER                  0x12 /* Power Control             */
404: #define SDIO_CCCR_HIGHSPEED              0x13 /* High-Speed                */
405: #define SDIO_CCCR_UHSI                   0x14 /* UHS-I Support             */
406: #define SDIO_CCCR_DRIVER                 0x15 /* Driver Strength           */
407: #define SDIO_CCCR_INTEXT                 0x16 /* Interrupt Extension       */
408: #define SDIO_CCCR_VENDOR                 0xF0 /* Reserved for Vendors      */
409: 
410: #define SDIO_CCCR_BUS_IF_WIDTH_MASK      0x03 /* Bus width configuration   */
411: #define SDIO_CCCR_BUS_IF_1_BIT           0x01 /* 1 bit bus width setting   */
412: #define SDIO_CCCR_BUS_IF_4_BITS          0x02 /* 4 bits bus width setting  */
413: 
414: #define SDIO_CCCR_HIGHSPEED_SHS          0x01 /* High-Speed mode capability */
415: #define SDIO_CCCR_HIGHSPEED_EHS          0x02 /* Enable High-Speed mode    */
416: 
417: #define SDIO_FBR_SHIFT   8                     /* FBR bit shift            */
418: #define SDIO_FN1_BR_BASE (1 << SDIO_FBR_SHIFT) /* Func 1 registers base    */

420: #define SDIO_FN3_BR_BASE (3 << SDIO_FBR_SHIFT) /* Func 3 registers base    */

423: #define SDIO_FN6_BR_BASE (6 << SDIO_FBR_SHIFT) /* Func 6 registers base    */

75: {
76:   uint32_t value;

78:   /* SYS_CPU_CLK_DIV_MODE2: SDIO divider [16:14], source [17]. */
79:   value = getreg32(0x44010024u);

86: static void sdio_reset_hw(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv)
87: {
88:   uint32_t value;
89: 
90:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK, 0);
91:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, 0xffffffffu);
92: 
93:   value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
94:   value &= ~(0xffffu | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
95:              BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_TX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET);
96:    value |= 0x0101u | BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_RECOVERY;
97:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
98: 
99:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
100:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
101:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT);
102:   sdio_set_clock(priv, BK7258_SDIO_ID_CLOCK);

105: static int sdio_wait_command(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv, uint32_t cmd)
106: {
107:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(1000);
108:   uint32_t status;
109: 
110:   for (;;)
111:     {
112:       status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
113:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
114:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
115:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
116:         {
117:           break;
118:         }
119: 
120:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
121:         {
122:           printf("SDIO CMD%u timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
123:                  (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
124:                  (unsigned long)status);
125:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
126:         }
127: 
128:       /* At transfer speed the RX FIFO can fill before a 100 us sleep
129:        * expires.  Keep the PIO loop tight while data is active; otherwise a
130:        * 512-byte sector consistently overflows after the first 256 bytes. */
131:       if (!priv->data_active)
132:         {
133:           nxsig_usleep(100);
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
138:              status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
139:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
140:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT |
141:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_OK |
142:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL));
143: 
144:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT) != 0)
145:     {
146:       printf("SDIO CMD%u response timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
147:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
148:              (unsigned long)status);
149:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
150:     }
151: 
152:   /* The BK7258 host reports CRC failure for the open-drain/long-response
153:    * identification commands even when the vendor stack accepts the response.
154:    * Armino explicitly tolerates this for ACMD41, CMD2 and CMD9.  Keep the
155:    * same compatibility rule while preserving CRC errors for normal R1/R7.
156:    */
157:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL) != 0 &&
158:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41 &&
159:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
160:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9)
161:     {
162:       printf("SDIO CMD%u CRC error status=0x%08lx\n",
163:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
164:              (unsigned long)status);
165:       return -EIO;
166:     }
167: 
168:   return OK;
169: }

171: static int sdio_sendcmd(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd,
172:                         uint32_t arg)
173: {
174:   uint32_t response;
175:   uint32_t value;
176: 
177:   response = (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) >> MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT;
178:   value = ((cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) << BK7258_SDIO_CMD_INDEX_SHIFT);
179:   if (response != MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE)
180:     {
181:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE;
182:     }
183:   if (response == MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE)
184:     {
185:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_LONG;
186:     }
187:   if (response != MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE &&
188:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
189:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9 &&
190:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41)
191:     {
192:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_CHECK;
193:     }
194: 
195:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_ARGUMENT, arg);
196:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_CMD_START);
197:   return OK;
198: }

269: static int mmcsd_lock(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv)
270: {
271:   int ret;
272: 
273:   /* Take the lock, giving exclusive access to the driver (perhaps
274:    * waiting)
275:    */
276: 
277:   if (!up_interrupt_context() && !sched_idletask())
278:     {
279:       ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
280:       if (ret < 0)
281:         {
282:           return ret;
283:         }
284: 
285:       /* Lock the bus if mutually exclusive access to the
286:        * SDIO bus is required on this platform.
287:        */
288: 
289: #ifdef CONFIG_SDIO_MUXBUS
290:       SDIO_LOCK(priv->dev, TRUE);
291: #endif
292:     }
293:   else
294:     {
295:       ret = OK;
296:     }
297: 
298:   return ret;
299: }
300: 
301: static void mmcsd_unlock(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv)
302: {
303:   if (!up_interrupt_context() && !sched_idletask())
304:     {
305:       /* Release the SDIO bus lock, then the MMC/SD driver mutex in the
306:        * opposite order that they were taken to assure that no deadlock
307:        * conditions will arise.
308:        */
309: 
310: #ifdef CONFIG_SDIO_MUXBUS
311:       SDIO_LOCK(priv->dev, FALSE);
312: #endif
313:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
314:     }
315: }

355:  *
356:  * Description:
357:  *   Set the Driver Stage Register (DSR) if (1) a CONFIG_MMCSD_DSR has been
358:  *   provided and (2) the card supports a DSR register.  If no DSR value
359:  *   the card default value (0x0404) will be used.
360:  *
361:  ****************************************************************************/

363: static inline int mmcsd_sendcmd4(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv)
364: {
365:   int ret = OK;
366: 
367: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_DSR
368:   /* The dsr_imp bit from the CSD will tell us if the card supports setting
369:    * the DSR via CMD4 or not.
370:    */
371: 
372:   if (priv->dsrimp != false)
373:     {
374:       finfo("Card supports DSR - send DSR.\n");
375:       /* CMD4 = SET_DSR will set the cards DSR register. The DSR and CMD4
376:        * support are optional.  However, since this is a broadcast command
377:        * with no response (like CMD0), we will never know if the DSR was
378:        * set correctly or not
379:        */
380: 
381:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD4, CONFIG_MMCSD_DSR << 16);
382:       MMCSD_USLEEP(MMCSD_DSR_DELAY);
383: 
384:       /* Send it again to have more confidence */
385: 
386:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD4, CONFIG_MMCSD_DSR << 16);
387:       MMCSD_USLEEP(MMCSD_DSR_DELAY);
388:     }
389:   else
390:     {
391:       finfo("Card does not support DSR.\n");
392:     }
393: #endif
394: 
395:   return ret;
396: }

574: 
575:   /* Word 1: Bits 127-96:
576:    *
577:    * CSD_STRUCTURE      127:126 CSD structure
578:    * SPEC_VERS          125:122 (MMC) Spec version
579:    * TAAC               119:112 Data read access-time-1
580:    *   TIME_VALUE         6:3   Time mantissa
581:    *   TIME_UNIT          2:0   Time exponent
582:    * NSAC               111:104 Data read access-time-2 in CLK
583:    *                            cycle(NSAC*100)
584:    * TRAN_SPEED         103:96  Max. data transfer rate
585:    *   TIME_VALUE         6:3   Rate exponent
586:    *   TRANSFER_RATE_UNIT 2:0   Rate mantissa
587:    */
588: 
589: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
590:   memset(&decoded, 0, sizeof(struct mmcsd_csd_s));
591:   decoded.csdstructure               =  csd[0] >> 30;
592:   decoded.mmcspecvers                = (csd[0] >> 26) & 0x0f;
593:   decoded.taac.timevalue             = (csd[0] >> 19) & 0x0f;
594:   decoded.taac.timeunit              = (csd[0] >> 16) & 7;
595:   decoded.nsac                       = (csd[0] >> 8)  & 0xff;
596:   decoded.transpeed.timevalue        = (csd[0] >> 3)  & 0x0f;
597:   decoded.transpeed.transferrateunit =  csd[0]        & 7;
598: #endif
599: 
600:   /* Word 2: Bits 64:95
601:    *   CCC                95:84 Card command classes
602:    *   READ_BL_LEN        83:80 Max. read data block length
603:    *   READ_BL_PARTIAL    79:79 Partial blocks for read allowed
604:    *   WRITE_BLK_MISALIGN 78:78 Write block misalignment
605:    *   READ_BLK_MISALIGN  77:77 Read block misalignment
606:    *   DSR_IMP            76:76 DSR implemented
607:    * Byte addressed SD and MMC:
608:    *   C_SIZE             73:62 Device size
609:    * Block addressed SD:
610:    *                      75:70 (reserved)
611:    *   C_SIZE             48:69 Device size
612:    */
613: 
614:   priv->dsrimp             = (csd[1] >> 12) & 1;
615:   readbllen                = (csd[1] >> 16) & 0x0f;
616: 
617: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
618:   decoded.ccc              = (csd[1] >> 20) & 0x0fff;
619:   decoded.readbllen        = (csd[1] >> 16) & 0x0f;
620:   decoded.readblpartial    = (csd[1] >> 15) & 1;
621:   decoded.writeblkmisalign = (csd[1] >> 14) & 1;
622:   decoded.readblkmisalign  = (csd[1] >> 13) & 1;
623:   decoded.dsrimp           = priv->dsrimp;
624: #endif
625: 
626:   /* Word 3: Bits 32-63
627:    *
628:    * Byte addressed SD:
629:    *   C_SIZE             73:62 Device size
630:    *   VDD_R_CURR_MIN     61:59 Max. read current at Vcc min
631:    *   VDD_R_CURR_MAX     58:56 Max. read current at Vcc max
632:    *   VDD_W_CURR_MIN     55:53 Max. write current at Vcc min
633:    *   VDD_W_CURR_MAX     52:50 Max. write current at Vcc max
634:    *   C_SIZE_MULT        49:47 Device size multiplier
635:    *   SD_ER_BLK_EN       46:46 Erase single block enable (SD only)
636:    *   SD_SECTOR_SIZE     45:39 Erase sector size
637:    *   SD_WP_GRP_SIZE     38:32 Write protect group size
638:    * Block addressed SD:
639:    *                      75:70 (reserved)
640:    *   C_SIZE             48:69 Device size
641:    *                      47:47 (reserved)
642:    *   SD_ER_BLK_EN       46:46 Erase single block enable (SD only)
643:    *   SD_SECTOR_SIZE     45:39 Erase sector size
644:    *   SD_WP_GRP_SIZE     38:32 Write protect group size
645:    * MMC:
646:    *   C_SIZE             73:62 Device size
647:    *   VDD_R_CURR_MIN     61:59 Max. read current at Vcc min
648:    *   VDD_R_CURR_MAX     58:56 Max. read current at Vcc max
649:    *   VDD_W_CURR_MIN     55:53 Max. write current at Vcc min
650:    *   VDD_W_CURR_MAX     52:50 Max. write current at Vcc max
651:    *   C_SIZE_MULT        49:47 Device size multiplier
652:    *   MMC_SECTOR_SIZE    46:42 Erase sector size
653:    *   MMC_ER_GRP_SIZE    41:37 Erase group size (MMC)
654:    *   MMC_WP_GRP_SIZE    36:32 Write protect group size
655:    */
656: 
657:   if (IS_BLOCK(priv->type))
658:     {
659: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT
660:       if (IS_MMC(priv->type))
661:         {
662:           /* Block addressed MMC:
663:            *
664:            * C_SIZE: 73:64 from Word 2 and 63:62 from Word 3
665:            */
666: 
667:           /* If the card is MMC and it has Block addressing, then C_SIZE
668:            * parameter is used to compute the device capacity for devices up
669:            * to 2 GB of density only, while SEC_COUNT is used to calculate
670:            * densities greater than 2 GB. When the device density is greater
671:            * than 2GB, 0xFFF should be set to C_SIZE bitfield (See 7.3.12)
672:            */
673: 
674:           uint16_t csize        = ((csd[1] & 0x03ff) << 2) |
675:                                   ((csd[2] >> 30) & 3);
676:           uint8_t  csizemult    = (csd[2] >> 15) & 7;
677: 
678:           priv->blockshift      = readbllen;
679:           priv->blocksize       = (1 << readbllen);
680: 
681:           /* For emmc densities up to 2 GB */
682: 
683:           if (csize != MMCSD_CSD_CSIZE_THRESHOLD)
684:             {
685:               priv->part[0].nblocks = ((uint32_t)csize + 1) *
686:                                       (1 << (csizemult + 2));
687:             }
688: 
689:           if (priv->blocksize > 512)
690:             {
691:               if (csize != MMCSD_CSD_CSIZE_THRESHOLD)
692:                 {
693:                   priv->part[0].nblocks <<= (priv->blockshift - 9);
694:                 }
695: 
696:               priv->blocksize   = 512;
697:               priv->blockshift  = 9;
698:             }
699: 
700: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
701:           decoded.u.mmc.csize               = csize;
702:           decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmin         = (csd[2] >> 27) & 7;
703:           decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmax         = (csd[2] >> 24) & 7;
704:           decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmin         = (csd[2] >> 21) & 7;
705:           decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmax         = (csd[2] >> 18) & 7;
706:           decoded.u.mmc.csizemult           = csizemult;
707:           decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.sectorsize = (csd[2] >> 10) & 0x1f;
708:           decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.ergrpsize  = (csd[2] >> 5) & 0x1f;
709:           decoded.u.mmc.mmcwpgrpsize        =  csd[2] & 0x1f;
710: #endif
711:         }
712:       else
713: #endif
714:         {
715:           /* Block addressed SD:
716:            *
717:            * C_SIZE: 69:64 from Word 2 and 63:48 from Word 3
718:            *
719:            *   512      = (1 << 9)
720:            *   1024     = (1 << 10)
721:            *   512*1024 = (1 << 19)
722:            */
723: 
724:           uint32_t csize        = ((csd[1] & 0x3f) << 16) | (csd[2] >> 16);
725: 
726:           priv->blockshift      = 9;
727:           priv->blocksize       = 1 << 9;
728:           priv->part[0].nblocks = (csize + 1) << (19 - priv->blockshift);
729: 
730: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
731:           decoded.u.sdblock.csize        = csize;
732:           decoded.u.sdblock.sderblen     = (csd[2] >> 14) & 1;
733:           decoded.u.sdblock.sdsectorsize = (csd[2] >> 7) & 0x7f;
734:           decoded.u.sdblock.sdwpgrpsize  =  csd[2] & 0x7f;
735: #endif
736:         }
737:     }
738:   else
739:     {
740:       /* Byte addressed SD:
741:        *
742:        * C_SIZE: 73:64 from Word 2 and 63:62 from Word 3
743:        */
744: 
745:       uint16_t csize            = ((csd[1] & 0x03ff) << 2) |
746:                                   ((csd[2] >> 30) & 3);
747:       uint8_t  csizemult        = (csd[2] >> 15) & 7;
748: 
749:       priv->part[0].nblocks     = ((uint32_t)csize + 1) *
750:                                   (1 << (csizemult + 2));
751:       priv->blockshift          = readbllen;
752:       priv->blocksize           = (1 << readbllen);
753: 
754:       /* Some devices, such as 2Gb devices, report blocksizes larger than
755:        * 512 bytes but still expect to be accessed with a 512 byte blocksize.
756:        *
757:        * NOTE: A minor optimization would be to eliminated priv->blocksize
758:        * and priv->blockshift:  Those values will be 512 and 9 in all cases
759:        * anyway.
760:        */
761: 
762:       if (priv->blocksize > 512)
763:         {
764:           priv->part[0].nblocks <<= (priv->blockshift - 9);
765:           priv->blocksize       = 512;
766:           priv->blockshift      = 9;
767:         }
768: 
769: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
770:       if (IS_SD(priv->type))
771:         {
772:           decoded.u.sdbyte.csize            = csize;
773:           decoded.u.sdbyte.vddrcurrmin      = (csd[2] >> 27) & 7;
774:           decoded.u.sdbyte.vddrcurrmax      = (csd[2] >> 24) & 7;
775:           decoded.u.sdbyte.vddwcurrmin      = (csd[2] >> 21) & 7;
776:           decoded.u.sdbyte.vddwcurrmax      = (csd[2] >> 18) & 7;
777:           decoded.u.sdbyte.csizemult        = csizemult;
778:           decoded.u.sdbyte.sderblen         = (csd[2] >> 14) & 1;
779:           decoded.u.sdbyte.sdsectorsize     = (csd[2] >> 7) & 0x7f;
780:           decoded.u.sdbyte.sdwpgrpsize      =  csd[2] & 0x7f;
781:         }
782: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT
783:       else if (IS_MMC(priv->type))
784:         {
785:           decoded.u.mmc.csize               = csize;
786:           decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmin         = (csd[2] >> 27) & 7;
787:           decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmax         = (csd[2] >> 24) & 7;
788:           decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmin         = (csd[2] >> 21) & 7;
789:           decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmax         = (csd[2] >> 18) & 7;
790:           decoded.u.mmc.csizemult           = csizemult;
791:           decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.sectorsize = (csd[2] >> 10) & 0x1f;
792:           decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.ergrpsize  = (csd[2] >> 5) & 0x1f;
793:           decoded.u.mmc.mmcwpgrpsize        =  csd[2] & 0x1f;
794:         }
795: #endif
796: #endif
797:     }
798: 
799:   /* Word 4: Bits 0-31
800:    *   WP_GRP_EN           31:31 Write protect group enable
801:    *   MMC DFLT_ECC        30:29 Manufacturer default ECC (MMC only)
802:    *   R2W_FACTOR          28:26 Write speed factor
803:    *   WRITE_BL_LEN        25:22 Max. write data block length
804:    *   WRITE_BL_PARTIAL    21:21 Partial blocks for write allowed
805:    *   FILE_FORMAT_GROUP   15:15 File format group
806:    *   COPY                14:14 Copy flag (OTP)
807:    *   PERM_WRITE_PROTECT  13:13 Permanent write protection
808:    *   TMP_WRITE_PROTECT   12:12 Temporary write protection
809:    *   FILE_FORMAT         10:11 File format
810:    *   ECC                  9:8  ECC (MMC only)
811:    *   CRC                  7:1  CRC
812:    *   Not used             0:0
813:    */
814: 
815:   permwriteprotect              = (csd[3] >> 13) & 1;
816:   tmpwriteprotect               = (csd[3] >> 12) & 1;
817:   priv->wrprotect               = (permwriteprotect || tmpwriteprotect);
818: 
819: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
820:   decoded.wpgrpen               =  csd[3] >> 31;
821:   decoded.mmcdfltecc            = (csd[3] >> 29) & 3;
822:   decoded.r2wfactor             = (csd[3] >> 26) & 7;
823:   decoded.writebllen            = (csd[3] >> 22) & 0x0f;
824:   decoded.writeblpartial        = (csd[3] >> 21) & 1;
825:   decoded.fileformatgrp         = (csd[3] >> 15) & 1;
826:   decoded.copy                  = (csd[3] >> 14) & 1;
827:   decoded.permwriteprotect      = permwriteprotect;
828:   decoded.tmpwriteprotect       = tmpwriteprotect;
829:   decoded.fileformat            = (csd[3] >> 10) & 3;
830:   decoded.mmcecc                = (csd[3] >> 8)  & 3;
831:   decoded.crc                   = (csd[3] >> 1)  & 0x7f;
832: 
833:   finfo("CSD:\n");
834:   finfo("  CSD_STRUCTURE: %d SPEC_VERS: %d (MMC)\n",
835:         decoded.csdstructure, decoded.mmcspecvers);
836:   finfo("  TAAC {TIME_UNIT: %d TIME_VALUE: %d} NSAC: %d\n",
837:         decoded.taac.timeunit, decoded.taac.timevalue, decoded.nsac);
838:   finfo("  TRAN_SPEED {TRANSFER_RATE_UNIT: %d TIME_VALUE: %d}\n",
839:         decoded.transpeed.transferrateunit, decoded.transpeed.timevalue);
840:   finfo("  CCC: %d\n", decoded.ccc);
841:   finfo("  READ_BL_LEN: %d READ_BL_PARTIAL: %d\n",
842:         decoded.readbllen, decoded.readblpartial);
843:   finfo("  WRITE_BLK_MISALIGN: %d READ_BLK_MISALIGN: %d\n",
844:         decoded.writeblkmisalign, decoded.readblkmisalign);
845:   finfo("  DSR_IMP: %d\n",
846:         decoded.dsrimp);
847: 
848:   if (IS_BLOCK(priv->type))
849:     {
850: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT
851:       if (IS_MMC(priv->type))
852:         {
853:           finfo("  MMC Block Addressing:\n");
854:           finfo("    C_SIZE: %d C_SIZE_MULT: %d\n",
855:                 decoded.u.mmc.csize, decoded.u.mmc.csizemult);
856:           finfo("    VDD_R_CURR_MIN: %d VDD_R_CURR_MAX: %d\n",
857:                 decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmin, decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmax);
858:           finfo("    VDD_W_CURR_MIN: %d VDD_W_CURR_MAX: %d\n",
859:                 decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmin, decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmax);
860:           finfo("    MMC_SECTOR_SIZE: %d MMC_ER_GRP_SIZE: %d "
861:                 "MMC_WP_GRP_SIZE: %d\n",
862:                 decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.sectorsize,
863:                 decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.ergrpsize,
864:                 decoded.u.mmc.mmcwpgrpsize);
865:         }
866:       else
867: #endif
868:         {
869:           finfo("  SD Block Addressing:\n");
870:           finfo("    C_SIZE: %d SD_ER_BLK_EN: %d\n",
871:                 decoded.u.sdblock.csize, decoded.u.sdblock.sderblen);
872:           finfo("    SD_SECTOR_SIZE: %d SD_WP_GRP_SIZE: %d\n",
873:                 decoded.u.sdblock.sdsectorsize,
874:                 decoded.u.sdblock.sdwpgrpsize);
875:         }
876:     }
877:   else if (IS_SD(priv->type))
878:     {
879:       finfo("  SD Byte Addressing:\n");
880:       finfo("    C_SIZE: %d C_SIZE_MULT: %d\n",
881:             decoded.u.sdbyte.csize, decoded.u.sdbyte.csizemult);
882:       finfo("    VDD_R_CURR_MIN: %d VDD_R_CURR_MAX: %d\n",
883:             decoded.u.sdbyte.vddrcurrmin, decoded.u.sdbyte.vddrcurrmax);
884:       finfo("    VDD_W_CURR_MIN: %d VDD_W_CURR_MAX: %d\n",
885:             decoded.u.sdbyte.vddwcurrmin, decoded.u.sdbyte.vddwcurrmax);
886:       finfo("    SD_ER_BLK_EN: %d SD_SECTOR_SIZE: %d (SD) "
887:             "SD_WP_GRP_SIZE: %d\n",
888:             decoded.u.sdbyte.sderblen, decoded.u.sdbyte.sdsectorsize,
889:             decoded.u.sdbyte.sdwpgrpsize);
890:     }
891: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT
892:   else if (IS_MMC(priv->type))
893:     {
894:       finfo("  MMC:\n");
895:       finfo("    C_SIZE: %d C_SIZE_MULT: %d\n",
896:             decoded.u.mmc.csize, decoded.u.mmc.csizemult);
897:       finfo("    VDD_R_CURR_MIN: %d VDD_R_CURR_MAX: %d\n",
898:             decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmin, decoded.u.mmc.vddrcurrmax);
899:       finfo("    VDD_W_CURR_MIN: %d VDD_W_CURR_MAX: %d\n",
900:             decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmin, decoded.u.mmc.vddwcurrmax);
901:       finfo("    MMC_SECTOR_SIZE: %d MMC_ER_GRP_SIZE: %d "
902:             "MMC_WP_GRP_SIZE: %d\n",
903:             decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.sectorsize,
904:             decoded.u.mmc.er.mmc22.ergrpsize,
905:             decoded.u.mmc.mmcwpgrpsize);
906:     }
907: #endif
908: 
909:   finfo("  WP_GRP_EN: %d MMC DFLT_ECC: %d (MMC) R2W_FACTOR: %d\n",
910:         decoded.wpgrpen, decoded.mmcdfltecc, decoded.r2wfactor);
911:   finfo("  WRITE_BL_LEN: %d WRITE_BL_PARTIAL: %d\n",
912:         decoded.writebllen, decoded.writeblpartial);
913:   finfo("  FILE_FORMAT_GROUP: %d COPY: %d\n",
914:         decoded.fileformatgrp, decoded.copy);
915:   finfo("  PERM_WRITE_PROTECT: %d TMP_WRITE_PROTECT: %d\n",
916:         decoded.permwriteprotect, decoded.tmpwriteprotect);
917:   finfo("  FILE_FORMAT: %d ECC: %d (MMC) CRC: %d\n",
918:         decoded.fileformat, decoded.mmcecc, decoded.crc);
919: 
920:   finfo("Capacity: %luKb, Block size: %db, nblocks: %d wrprotect: %d\n",
921:         (unsigned long)MMCSD_CAPACITY(priv->part[0].nblocks,
922:                                       priv->blockshift),
923:         priv->blocksize, priv->part[0].nblocks, priv->wrprotect);
924: #endif
925: }

927: /****************************************************************************
928:  * Name: mmcsd_decode_cid
929:  *
930:  * Description:
931:  *   Show the contents of the Card Identification Data (CID) (for debug
932:  *   purposes only)
933:  *
934:  ****************************************************************************/
935: 
936: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
937: static void mmcsd_decode_cid(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv, uint32_t cid[4])
938: {
939:   struct mmcsd_cid_s decoded;
940: 
941:   /* Word 1: Bits 127-96:
942:    *   mid - 127-120  8-bit Manufacturer ID
943:    *   cbx - 113-112  2-bit Device/BGA
944:    *   oid - 111-104  8-bit OEM/Application ID (ascii)
945:    *   pnm - 103-56   48-bit Product Name (ascii) + null terminator
946:    *         pnm[0] 103:96
947:    */
948: 
949:   decoded.mid    =  cid[0] >> 24;
950:   decoded.cbx    = (cid[0] >> 16) & 0x3;
951:   decoded.oid    = (cid[0] >> 8) & 0xff;
952:   decoded.pnm[0] =  cid[0] & 0xff;
953: 
954:   /* Word 2: Bits 64:95
955:    *   pnm - 103-56  48-bit Product Name (ascii) + null terminator
956:    *         pnm[1] 95:88
957:    *         pnm[2] 87:80
958:    *         pnm[3] 79:72
959:    *         pnm[4] 71:64
960:    */
961: 
962:   decoded.pnm[1] =  cid[1] >> 24;
963:   decoded.pnm[2] = (cid[1] >> 16) & 0xff;
964:   decoded.pnm[3] = (cid[1] >> 8) & 0xff;
965:   decoded.pnm[4] =  cid[1] & 0xff;
966: 
967:   /* Word 3: Bits 32-63
968:    *         pnm[5] 63-56
969:    *   prv    -  55-48   8-bit Product revision
970:    *   psn    -  47-16   32-bit Product serial number
971:    *         psn 47-32
972:    */
973: 
974:   decoded.pnm[5] = cid[2] >> 24;
975:   decoded.pnm[6] = '\0';
976:   decoded.prv    = (cid[2] >> 16) & 0xff;
977:   decoded.psn    = cid[2] << 16;
978: 
979:   /* Word 4: Bits 0-31
980:    *          psn 31-16
981:    *   mdt -  15:8    8-bit Manufacturing date
982:    *   crc -   7:1    7-bit CRC7
983:    */
984: 
985:   decoded.psn   |=  cid[3] >> 16;
986:   decoded.mdt    = (cid[3] >> 8) & 0xff;
987:   decoded.crc    = (cid[3] >> 1) & 0x7f;
988: 
989:   finfo("mid: %02x cbx: %01x oid: %01x pnm: %s prv: %d psn: %08x mdt: %02x\
990:          crc: %02x\n", decoded.mid, decoded.cbx, decoded.oid, decoded.pnm,
991:          decoded.prv, (unsigned long)decoded.psn, decoded.mdt, decoded.crc);
992: }
993: #endif

995: /****************************************************************************
996:  * Name: mmcsd_decode_scr
997:  *
998:  * Description:
999:  *   Show the contents of the SD Configuration Register (SCR).  The only
1000:  *   value retained is:  priv->buswidth;
1001:  *
1002:  ****************************************************************************/
1003: 
1004: static void mmcsd_decode_scr(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv, uint32_t scr[2])
1005: {
1006: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
1007:   struct mmcsd_scr_s decoded;
1008: #endif
1009: 
1010:   /* Word 1, bits 63:32
1011:    *   SCR_STRUCTURE          63:60 4-bit SCR structure version
1012:    *   SD_VERSION             59:56 4-bit SD memory spec. version
1013:    *   DATA_STATE_AFTER_ERASE 55:55 1-bit erase status
1014:    *   SD_SECURITY            54:52 3-bit SD security support level
1015:    *   SD_BUS_WIDTHS          51:48 4-bit bus width indicator
1016:    *   Reserved               47:34 14-bit SD reserved space
1017:    *   CMD_SUPPORT            33:32 2-bit command supported (bit33 for cmd23)
1018:    */
1019: 
1020: #ifdef CONFIG_ENDIAN_BIG  /* Card transfers SCR in big-endian order */
1021:   priv->buswidth     = (scr[0] >> 16) & 15;
1022:   priv->cmd23support = (scr[0] >> 1)  & 1;
1023: #else
1024:   priv->buswidth     = (scr[0] >> 8)  & 15;
1025:   priv->cmd23support = (scr[0] >> 25) & 1;
1026: #endif
1027: 
1028: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FS_INFO
1029: #ifdef CONFIG_ENDIAN_BIG

1130:  *

1133: static int mmcsd_get_r1(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv, FAR uint32_t *r1)
1134: {
1135:   uint32_t local_r1;
1136:   int ret;
1137: 
1138:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && r1 != NULL);

1140:   /* Send CMD13, SEND_STATUS.  The addressed card responds by sending its
1141:    * R1 card status register.
1142:    */

1144:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD13, (uint32_t)priv->rca << 16);
1145:   ret = SDIO_RECVR1(priv->dev, MMCSD_CMD13, &local_r1);
1146:   if (ret == OK)

1148:       /* Check if R1 reports an error */

1150:       if ((local_r1 & MMCSD_R1_ERRORMASK) != 0)
1151:         {
1152:           /* Card locked is considered an error. Save the card locked
1153:            * indication for later use.
1154:            */

1157:

1161:                 local_r1);
1162:           ret = -EIO;
1163:         }
1164:       else
1165:         {
1166:           /* No errors, return R1 */

1169:         }

1242: static int mmcsd_eventwait(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv,
1243:                            sdio_eventset_t failevents)
1244: {
1245:   sdio_eventset_t wkupevent;

1247:   /* Wait for the set of events enabled by SDIO_EVENTENABLE. */

1252:    * the wait.  It should always be non-zero, but may contain failure as

1262:     }

1265:    * (or more) success events.
1266:    */

1271: /****************************************************************************
1272:  * Name: mmcsd_transferready
1273:  *
1274:  * Description:
1275:  *   Check if the MMC/SD card is ready for the next read or write transfer.
1276:  *   Ready means:  (1) card still in the slot, and (2) if the last transfer
1277:  *   was a write transfer, the card is no longer busy from that transfer.
1278:  *
1279:  ****************************************************************************/
1280: 
1281: static int mmcsd_transferready(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv)
1282: {
1283:   clock_t starttime;
1284:   clock_t elapsed;
1285:   uint32_t r1;
1286:   int ret;
1287: 
1288:   /* First, check if the card has been removed. */
1289: 
1290:   if (IS_EMPTY(priv) || !SDIO_PRESENT(priv->dev))
1291:     {
1292:       ferr("ERROR: Card has been removed\n");
1293:       return -ENODEV;
1294:     }
1295: 
1296:   /* If the last data transfer was not a write, then we do not have to check
1297:    * the card status.
1298:    */
1299: 
1300:   else if (!priv->wrbusy)
1301:     {
1302:       return OK;
1303:     }
1304: 
1305:   /* The card is still present and the last transfer was a write transfer.
1306:    * Loop, querying the card state.  Return when (1) the card is in the
1307:    * TRANSFER state, (2) the card stays in the PROGRAMMING state too long,
1308:    * or (3) the card is in any other state.
1309:    *
1310:    * The PROGRAMMING state occurs normally after a WRITE operation.  During
1311:    * this time, the card may be busy completing the WRITE and is not
1312:    * available for other operations.  The card will transition from the
1313:    * PROGRAMMING state to the TRANSFER state when the card completes the
1314:    * WRITE operation.
1315:    */
1316: 
1317: #if defined(CONFIG_MMCSD_SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE)
1318:   ret = mmcsd_eventwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
1319:   if (ret != OK)
1320:     {
1321:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_eventwait for transfer ready failed: %d\n", ret);
1322:     }
1323: #endif
1324: 
1325:   starttime = clock_systime_ticks();
1326:   do
1327:     {
1328:       /* Get the current R1 status from the card */
1329: 
1330:       ret = mmcsd_get_r1(priv, &r1);
1331:       if (ret != OK)
1332:         {
1333:           ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_get_r1 failed: %d\n", ret);
1334:           return ret;
1335:         }
1336: 
1337:       /* Now check if the card is in the expected transfer state. */
1338: 
1339:       if (IS_STATE(r1, MMCSD_R1_STATE_TRAN))
1340:         {
1341:           /* Yes.. return Success */
1342: 
1343:           priv->wrbusy = false;
1344:           return OK;
1345:         }
1346: 
1347:       /* Check for the programming state. This is not an error.  It means
1348:        * that the card is still busy from the last (write) transfer.  The
1349:        * card can also still be receiving data, for example, if hardware
1350:        * receive FIFOs are not yet empty.
1351:        */
1352: 
1353:       else if (!IS_STATE(r1, MMCSD_R1_STATE_PRG) &&
1354:                !IS_STATE(r1, MMCSD_R1_STATE_RCV))
1355:         {
1356:           /* Any other state would be an error in this context.  There is
1357:            * a possibility that the card is not selected.  In this case,
1358:            * it could be in STANDBY or DISCONNECTED state and the fix
1359:            * might be to send CMD7 to re-select the card.  Consider this
1360:            * if this error occurs.
1361:            */
1362: 
1363:           ferr("ERROR: Unexpected R1 state: %08" PRIx32 "\n", r1);
1364:           return -EINVAL;
1365:         }
1366: 
1367:       /* Do not hog the CPU */
1368: 
1369: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_CHECK_READY_STATUS_WITHOUT_SLEEP
1370:       /* Use sched_yield when tick is big to avoid low writing speed */
1371: 
1372:       sched_yield();
1373: #else
1374:       MMCSD_USLEEP(1000);
1375: #endif
1376: 
1377:       /* We are still in the programming state. Calculate the elapsed
1378:        * time... we can't stay in this loop forever!
1379:        */
1380: 
1381:       elapsed = clock_systime_ticks() - starttime;
1382:     }
1383:   while (elapsed < TICK_PER_SEC);
1384: 
1385:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
1386: }

1476: /****************************************************************************
1477:  * Name: mmcsd_readsingle
1478:  *
1479:  * Description:
1480:  *   Read a single block of data.
1481:  *
1482:  ****************************************************************************/
1483: 
1484: static ssize_t mmcsd_readsingle(FAR struct mmcsd_part_s *part,
1485:                                 FAR uint8_t *buffer, off_t startblock)
1486: {
1487:   FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv = part->priv;
1488:   uint32_t partnum = part - priv->part;
1489:   off_t offset;
1490:   int ret;
1491: 
1492:   finfo("startblock=%jd\n", (intmax_t)startblock);
1493:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && buffer != NULL);
1494: 
1495:   /* Check if the card is locked */
1496: 
1497:   if (priv->locked)
1498:     {
1499:       ferr("ERROR: Card is locked\n");
1500:       return -EPERM;
1501:     }
1502: 
1503:   if (priv->partnum != partnum)
1504:     {
1505:       ret = mmcsd_switch(priv, MMC_CMD6_MODE(MMC_CMD6_MODE_WRITE_BYTE) |
1506:                                MMC_CMD6_INDEX(EXT_CSD_PART_CONF) |
1507:                                MMC_CMD6_VALUE(partnum));
1508:       if (ret != OK)
1509:         {
1510:           ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_switch failed: %d\n", ret);
1511:           return ret;
1512:         }
1513: 
1514:       priv->partnum = partnum;
1515:     }
1516: 
1517: #if defined(CONFIG_SDIO_DMA) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_SDIO_PREFLIGHT)
1518:   /* If we think we are going to perform a DMA transfer, make sure that we
1519:    * will be able to before we commit the card to the operation.
1520:    */
1521: 
1522:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
1523:     {
1524:       ret = SDIO_DMAPREFLIGHT(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
1525: 
1526:       if (ret != OK)
1527:         {
1528:           return ret;
1529:         }
1530:     }
1531: #endif
1532: 
1533:   /* Verify that the card is ready for the transfer.  The card may still be
1534:    * busy from the preceding write transfer.  It would be simpler to check
1535:    * for write busy at the end of each write, rather than at the beginning of
1536:    * each read AND write, but putting the busy-wait at the beginning of the
1537:    * transfer allows for more overlap and, hopefully, better performance
1538:    */
1539: 
1540:   ret = mmcsd_transferready(priv);
1541:   if (ret != OK)
1542:     {
1543:       ferr("ERROR: Card not ready: %d\n", ret);
1544:       return ret;
1545:     }
1546: 
1547:   /* If this is a byte addressed SD card, then convert sector start sector
1548:    * number to a byte offset
1549:    */
1550: 
1551:   if (IS_BLOCK(priv->type))
1552:     {
1553:       offset = startblock;
1554:     }
1555:   else
1556:     {
1557:       offset = startblock << priv->blockshift;
1558:     }
1559: 
1560:   finfo("offset=%jd\n", (intmax_t)offset);
1561: 
1562:   /* Select the block size for the card */
1563: 
1564:   ret = mmcsd_setblocklen(priv, priv->blocksize);
1565:   if (ret != OK)
1566:     {
1567:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_setblocklen failed: %d\n", ret);
1568:       return ret;
1569:     }
1570: 
1571:   /* Configure SDIO controller hardware for the read transfer */
1572: 
1573:   SDIO_BLOCKSETUP(priv->dev, priv->blocksize, 1);
1574:   SDIO_WAITENABLE(priv->dev,
1575:                   SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR,
1576:                   MMCSD_BLOCK_RDATADELAY);
1577: 
1578: #ifdef CONFIG_SDIO_DMA
1579:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
1580:     {
1581:       ret = SDIO_DMARECVSETUP(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
1582:       if (ret != OK)
1583:         {
1584:           finfo("SDIO_DMARECVSETUP: error %d\n", ret);
1585:           SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
1586:           return ret;
1587:         }
1588:     }
1589:   else
1590: #endif
1591:     {
1592:       SDIO_RECVSETUP(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
1593:     }
1594: 
1595:   /* Send CMD17, READ_SINGLE_BLOCK: Read a block of the size selected
1596:    * by the mmcsd_setblocklen() and verify that good R1 status is
1597:    * returned.  The card state should change from Transfer to Sending-Data
1598:    * state.
1599:    */
1600: 
1601:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD17, offset);
1602:   ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD17);
1603:   if (ret != OK)
1604:     {
1605:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_recv_r1 for CMD17 failed: %d\n", ret);
1606:       SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
1607:       return ret;
1608:     }
1609: 
1610:   /* Then wait for the data transfer to complete */
1611: 
1612:   ret = mmcsd_eventwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
1613:   if (ret != OK)
1614:     {
1615:       ferr("ERROR: CMD17 transfer failed: %d\n", ret);
1616:       return ret;
1617:     }
1618: 
1619:   /* Return value:  One sector read */
1620: 
1621:   return 1;
1622: }

2330:  *   Read the specified number of sectors from the read-ahead buffer or from
2331:  *   the physical device.
2332:  *
2333:  ****************************************************************************/
2334: 
2335: static ssize_t mmcsd_read(FAR struct inode *inode, unsigned char *buffer,
2336:                           blkcnt_t startsector, unsigned int nsectors)
2337: {
2338:   FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv;
2339:   FAR struct mmcsd_part_s *part;
2340:   size_t sector;
2341:   size_t endsector;
2342:   ssize_t nread;
2343:   ssize_t ret = nsectors;
2344: 
2345:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
2346:   part = inode->i_private;
2347:   priv = part->priv;
2348: 
2349:   finfo("startsector: %" PRIuOFF " nsectors: %u sectorsize: %d\n",
2350:         startsector, nsectors, priv->blocksize);
2351: 
2352:   if (nsectors > 0)
2353:     {
2354:       ret = mmcsd_lock(priv);
2355:       if (ret < 0)
2356:         {
2357:           return ret;
2358:         }
2359: 
2360:       ret = nsectors;
2361:       endsector = startsector + nsectors;
2362:       for (sector = startsector; sector < endsector; sector += nread)
2363:         {
2364:           /* Read this sector into the user buffer */
2365: 
2366: #if MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT == 1
2367:           /* Read each block using only the single block transfer method */
2368: 
2369:           nread = mmcsd_readsingle(part, buffer, sector);
2370: #else
2371:           nread = endsector - sector;
2372:           if (nread > MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT)
2373:             {
2374:               nread = MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT;
2375:             }
2376: 
2377:           if (nread == 1)
2378:             {
2379:               nread = mmcsd_readsingle(part, buffer, sector);
2380:             }
2381:           else
2382:             {
2383:               nread = mmcsd_readmultiple(part, buffer, sector, nread);
2384:             }
2385: 
2386: #endif
2387:           if (nread < 0)
2388:             {
2389:               ret = nread;
2390:               break;
2391:             }
2392: 
2393:           /* Increment the buffer pointer by the sector size */
2394: 
2395:           buffer += nread * priv->blocksize;
2396:         }
2397: 
2398:       mmcsd_unlock(priv);
2399:     }
2400: 
2401:   /* On success, return the number of blocks read */
2402: 
2403:   return ret;
2404: }

2650:  * Name: mmcsd_mediachange
2651:  *
2652:  * Description:
2653:  *  This is a callback function from the SDIO driver that indicates that
2654:  *  there has been a change in the slot... either a card has been inserted
2655:  *  or a card has been removed.
2656:  *
2657:  * Assumptions:
2658:  *   This callback is NOT supposd to run in the context of an interrupt
2659:  *   handler; it is probably running in the context of work thread.
2660:  *
2661:  ****************************************************************************/
2662: 
2663: static void mmcsd_mediachange(FAR void *arg)
2664: {
2665:   FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv = (FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *)arg;
2666:   int ret;
2667: 
2668:   finfo("arg: %p\n", arg);
2669:   DEBUGASSERT(priv);
2670: 
2671:   /* Is there a card present in the slot? */
2672: 
2673:   ret = mmcsd_lock(priv);
2674:   if (ret < 0)
2675:     {
2676:       return;
2677:     }
2678: 
2679:   if (SDIO_PRESENT(priv->dev))
2680:     {
2681:       /* Yes... process the card insertion.  This could cause chaos if we
2682:        * think that a card is already present and there are mounted file
2683:        * systems!  NOTE that mmcsd_probe() will always re-enable callbacks
2684:        * appropriately.
2685:        */
2686: 
2687:       mmcsd_probe(priv);
2688:     }
2689:   else
2690:     {
2691:       /* No... process the card removal.  This could have very bad
2692:        * implications for any mounted file systems!  NOTE that
2693:        * mmcsd_removed() does NOT re-enable callbacks so we will need to
2694:        * do that here.
2695:        */
2696: 
2697:       mmcsd_removed(priv);
2698: 
2699:       /* Enable logic to detect if a card is re-inserted */
2700: 
2701:       SDIO_CALLBACKENABLE(priv->dev, SDIOMEDIA_INSERTED);
2702:     }
2703: 
2704:   mmcsd_unlock(priv);
2705: }

2707: /****************************************************************************
2708:  * Name: mmcsd_widebus
2709:  *
2710:  * Description:
2711:  *  An SD card has been inserted and its SCR has been obtained.  Select wide
2712:  *  (4-bit) bus operation if the card supports it.
2713:  *
2714:  * Assumptions:
2715:  *   This function is called only once per card insertion as part of the SD
2716:  *   card initialization sequence.  It is not necessary to reselect the card
2717:  *   there is not need to check if wide bus operation has already been
2718:  *   selected.
2719:  *
2720:  ****************************************************************************/
2721: 
2722: static int mmcsd_widebus(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv)
2723: {
2724:   int ret;
2725: 
2726:   /* Check if the SD card supports wide bus operation (as reported in the
2727:    * SCR or in the SDIO driver capabililities)
2728:    */
2729: 
2730:   if (IS_SD(priv->type) &&
2731:       (priv->buswidth & MMCSD_SCR_BUSWIDTH_4BIT) != 0 &&
2732:       (priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_1BIT_ONLY) == 0)
2733:     {
2734:       /* SD card supports 4-bit BUS and host settings is not 1-bit only. */
2735: 
2736:       finfo("Setting SD BUS width to 4-bit. Card type: %d\n", priv->type);
2737: 
2738:       /* Disconnect any CD/DAT3 pull up using ACMD42.  ACMD42 is optional and
2739:        * need not be supported by all SD calls.
2740:        *
2741:        * First end CMD55 APP_CMD with argument as card's RCA.
2742:        */
2743: 
2744:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, SD_CMD55, (uint32_t)priv->rca << 16);
2745:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, SD_CMD55);
2746:       if (ret != OK)
2747:         {
2748:           ferr("ERROR: RECVR1 for CMD55 of ACMD42: %d\n", ret);
2749:           return ret;
2750:         }
2751: 
2752:       /* Then send ACMD42 with the argument to disconnect the CD/DAT3
2753:        * pull-up
2754:        *
2755:        * TODO: May want to disable, then re-enable around data transfers
2756:        * to support card detection"
2757:        */
2758: 
2759:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, SD_ACMD42, MMCSD_ACMD42_CD_DISCONNECT);
2760:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, SD_ACMD42);
2761:       if (ret != OK)
2762:         {
2763:           fwarn("WARNING: SD card does not support ACMD42: %d\n", ret);
2764:           return ret;
2765:         }
2766: 
2767:       /* Now send ACMD6 to select bus width operation, beginning
2768:        * with CMD55, APP_CMD:
2769:        */
2770: 
2771:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, SD_CMD55, (uint32_t)priv->rca << 16);
2772:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, SD_CMD55);
2773:       if (ret != OK)
2774:         {
2775:           ferr("ERROR: RECVR1 for CMD55 of ACMD6: %d\n", ret);
2776:           return ret;
2777:         }
2778: 
2779:       /* Then send ACMD6 */
2780: 
2781:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, SD_ACMD6, MMCSD_ACMD6_BUSWIDTH_4);
2782: 
2783:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, SD_ACMD6);
2784:       if (ret != OK)
2785:         {
2786:           return ret;
2787:         }
2788:     }
2789: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT
2790:   else if (IS_MMC(priv->type) &&
2791:            ((priv->buswidth & MMCSD_SCR_BUSWIDTH_4BIT) != 0 &&
2792:            (priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_1BIT_ONLY) == 0))
2793:     {
2794:       /* SD card supports 4-bit BUS and host settings is not 1-bit only.
2795:        * Configuring MMC - Use MMC_SWITCH access modes.
2796:        */
2797: 
2798:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD6,
2799:                         MMC_CMD6_BUSWIDTH(EXT_CSD_BUS_WIDTH_4));
2800:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD6);
2801: 
2802:       if (ret != OK)
2803:         {
2804:           ferr("ERROR: (MMCSD_CMD6) Setting MMC BUS width: %d\n", ret);
2805:           return ret;
2806:         }
2807:     }
2808: #endif /* #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT */
2809:   else if (!IS_SD(priv->type) && !IS_MMC(priv->type))
2810:     {
2811:       /* Take this path when no MMC / SD is yet detected */
2812: 
2813:       fwarn("No card inserted.\n");
2814:       SDIO_WIDEBUS(priv->dev, false);
2815:       priv->widebus = false;
2816:       SDIO_CLOCK(priv->dev, CLOCK_SDIO_DISABLED);
2817:       MMCSD_USLEEP(MMCSD_CLK_DELAY);
2818: 
2819:       return OK;
2820:     }
2821: 
2822:   /* Configure the SDIO peripheral */
2823: 
2824:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_1BIT_ONLY) == 0 &&
2825:       (IS_MMC(priv->type) ||
2826:        (priv->buswidth & MMCSD_SCR_BUSWIDTH_4BIT) != 0))
2827:     {
2828:       /* JEDEC specs: A.8.3 Changing the data bus width: 'Bus testing
2829:        * procedure' shows how mmc bus width may be detected.  This driver
2830:        * doesn't do it, so let the low level driver decide how to go with
2831:        * the widebus selection.  It may well be 1, 4 or 8 bits.
2832:        *
2833:        * For SD cards the priv->buswidth is set.
2834:        */
2835: 
2836:       finfo("Wide bus operation selected\n");
2837:       SDIO_WIDEBUS(priv->dev, true);
2838:       priv->widebus = true;
2839:     }
2840:   else
2841:     {
2842:       finfo("Narrow bus operation selected\n");
2843:       SDIO_WIDEBUS(priv->dev, false);
2844:       priv->widebus = false;
2845:     }
2846: 
2847:   if (IS_SD(priv->type))
2848:     {
2849:       if ((priv->buswidth & MMCSD_SCR_BUSWIDTH_4BIT) != 0)
2850:         {
2851:           SDIO_CLOCK(priv->dev, CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_4BIT);
2852:         }
2853:       else
2854:         {
2855:           SDIO_CLOCK(priv->dev, CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_1BIT);
2856:         }
2857:     }
2858: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT
2859:   else
2860:     {
2861:       if (priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_MMC_HS_MODE)
2862:         {
2863:           mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD6,
2864:                             MMC_CMD6_HS_TIMING(EXT_CSD_HS_TIMING_HS));
2865:           ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD6);
2866:           if (ret != OK)
2867:             {
2868:               ferr("ERROR: (MMCSD_CMD6) Setting MMC speed mode: %d\n", ret);
2869:               return ret;
2870:             }
2871: 
2872:           priv->mode = EXT_CSD_HS_TIMING_HS;
2873:         }
2874: 
2875:       SDIO_CLOCK(priv->dev, CLOCK_MMC_TRANSFER);
2876:     }
2877: #endif /* #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT */
2878: 
2879:   MMCSD_USLEEP(MMCSD_CLK_DELAY);
2880:   return OK;
2881: }

2884: /****************************************************************************
2885:  * Name: mmcsd_decode_extcsd
2886:  *
2887:  * Description:
2888:  *   Get all partitions size in block numbers
2889:  *
2890:  ****************************************************************************/
2891: 
2892: static void mmcsd_decode_extcsd(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv,
2893:                                 FAR const uint8_t *extcsd)
2894: {
2895:   uint8_t hc_erase_grp_sz;
2896:   uint8_t hc_wp_grp_sz;
2897:   int idx;
2898: 
2899:   /* User data partition size = SEC_COUNT x 512B for densities greater
2900:    * than 2 GB
2901:    */
2902: 
2903:   priv->part[0].nblocks = (extcsd[215] << 24) | (extcsd[214] << 16) |
2904:                           (extcsd[213] << 8) | extcsd[212];
2905:   finfo("MMC ext CSD read succsesfully, number of block %" PRIuOFF "\n",
2906:                                                 priv->part[0].nblocks);
2907: 
2908:   if (extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_PARTITION_SUPPORT] & MMCSD_PART_SUPPORT_PART_EN)
2909:     {
2910:       /* Boot partition size = 128KB byte x BOOT_SIZE_MULT */
2911: 
2912:       priv->part[MMCSD_PART_BOOT0].nblocks =
2913:             extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_BOOT_SIZE_MULT] * MCSD_SZ_128K / MCSD_SZ_512;
2914:       priv->part[MMCSD_PART_BOOT1].nblocks =
2915:             extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_BOOT_SIZE_MULT] * MCSD_SZ_128K / MCSD_SZ_512;
2916: 
2917:       /* RPMB partition size = 128KB byte x RPMB_SIZE_MULT */
2918: 
2919:       priv->part[MMCSD_PART_RPMB].nblocks =
2920:             extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_RPMB_SIZE_MULT] * MCSD_SZ_128K / MCSD_SZ_512;
2921: 
2922:       hc_erase_grp_sz = extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_HC_ERASE_GRP_SIZE];
2923:       hc_wp_grp_sz = extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_HC_WP_GRP_SIZE];
2924: 
2925:       for (idx = 0; idx < 4; idx++)
2926:         {
2927:           if (!extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_GP_SIZE_MULT + idx * 3] &&
2928:               !extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_GP_SIZE_MULT + idx * 3 + 1] &&
2929:               !extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_GP_SIZE_MULT + idx * 3 + 2])
2930:             {
2931:               continue;
2932:             }
2933: 
2934:           if (extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_PARTITION_SETTING_COMPLETED] == 0)
2935:             {
2936:               finfo("Partition size defined without setting complete!\n");
2937:               break;
2938:             }
2939: 
2940:           /* General purpose partition size = (GP_SIZE_MULT_X_2 << 16 +
2941:            *  GP_SIZE_MULT_X_1 << 8 + GP_SIZE_MULT_X_0) x HC_WP_GRP_SIZE x
2942:            *  HC_ERASE_GRP_SIZE x 512kBytes
2943:            */
2944: 
2945:           priv->part[MMCSD_PART_GENP0 + idx].nblocks =
2946:                 ((extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_GP_SIZE_MULT + idx * 3 + 2] << 16) +
2947:                  (extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_GP_SIZE_MULT + idx * 3 + 1] << 8) +
2948:                  extcsd[MMCSD_EXTCSD_GP_SIZE_MULT + idx * 3]) *
2949:                 hc_erase_grp_sz * hc_wp_grp_sz * MCSD_SZ_512K / MCSD_SZ_512;
2950:         }
2951:     }
2952: }

2954: /****************************************************************************
2955:  * Name: mmcsd_mmcinitialize
2956:  *
2957:  * Description:
2958:  *   We believe that there is an MMC card in the slot.  Attempt to initialize
2959:  *   and configure the MMC card.  This is called only from mmcsd_probe().
2960:  *
2961:  ****************************************************************************/
2962: 
2963: static int mmcsd_mmcinitialize(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv)
2964: {
2965:   uint8_t extcsd[512] aligned_data(16);
2966:   int ret;
2967: 
2968:   /* At this point, slow, ID mode clocking has been supplied to the card
2969:    * and CMD0 has been sent successfully. CMD1 succeeded and ACMD41 failed
2970:    * so there is good evidence that we have an MMC card inserted into the
2971:    * slot.
2972:    *
2973:    * Send CMD2, ALL_SEND_CID. This implementation supports only one MMC
2974:    * slot.  If multiple cards were installed, each card would respond to
2975:    * CMD2 by sending its CID (only one card completes the response at a
2976:    * time).  The driver should send CMD2 and assign an RCAs until no
2977:    * response to ALL_SEND_CID is received. CMD2 causes transition to
2978:    * identification state / card-identification mode.
2979:    */
2980: 
2981:   finfo("Initialising MMC card.\n");
2982: 
2983:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD2, 0);
2984:   ret = SDIO_RECVR2(priv->dev, MMCSD_CMD2, priv->cid);
2985:   if (ret != OK)
2986:     {
2987:       ferr("ERROR: SDIO_RECVR2 for MMC CID failed: %d\n", ret);
2988:       return ret;
2989:     }
2990: 
2991:   mmcsd_decode_cid(priv, priv->cid);
2992: 
2993:   /* Send CMD3, SET_RELATIVE_ADDR.  This command is used to assign a logical
2994:    * address to the card.  For MMC, the host assigns the address. CMD3 causes
2995:    * transition to standby state/data-transfer mode
2996:    */
2997: 
2998:   priv->rca = 1;  /* There is only one card */
2999:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMC_CMD3, (uint32_t)priv->rca << 16);
3000:   ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMC_CMD3);
3001:   if (ret != OK)
3002:     {
3003:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_recv_r1(CMD3) failed: %d\n", ret);
3004:       return ret;
3005:     }
3006: 
3007:   /* This should have caused a transition to standby state. However, this
3008:    * will not be reflected in the present R1/6 status.  R1/6 contains the
3009:    * state of the card when the command was received, not when it
3010:    * completed execution.
3011:    *
3012:    * Verify that we are in standby state/data-transfer mode
3013:    */
3014: 
3015:   ret = mmcsd_verifystate(priv, MMCSD_R1_STATE_STBY);
3016:   if (ret != OK)
3017:     {
3018:       ferr("ERROR: Failed to enter standby state\n");
3019:       return ret;
3020:     }
3021: 
3022:   /* Send CMD9, SEND_CSD in standby state/data-transfer mode to obtain the
3023:    * Card Specific Data (CSD) register, e.g., block length, card storage
3024:    * capacity, etc. (Stays in standby state/data-transfer mode).
3025:    * NOTE in v2.0 high capacity cards, the following values are always
3026:    * returned:
3027:    *  - write block length = 9 = 2^9 = 512
3028:    *  - read block length = 9 = 512
3029:    *  - rw2 factor = 0x2 (010b)
3030:    *  - size_mult = 0
3031:    * We can't decode the CSD register yet as we also need to read the
3032:    * extended CSD register.
3033:    */
3034: 
3035:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD9, (uint32_t)priv->rca << 16);
3036:   ret = SDIO_RECVR2(priv->dev, MMCSD_CMD9, priv->csd);
3037:   if (ret != OK)
3038:     {
3039:       ferr("ERROR: Could not get SD CSD register: %d\n", ret);
3040:       return ret;
3041:     }
3042: 
3043:   /* Decode the CSD register to obtain version.  We will need to
3044:    * decode further if card is v4.0 or higher as it supports
3045:    * ext_csd commands.
3046:    */
3047: 
3048:   mmcsd_decode_csd(priv, priv->csd);
3049: 
3050:   /* Set the Driver Stage Register (DSR) if (1) a CONFIG_MMCSD_DSR has been
3051:    * provided and (2) the card supports a DSR register.  If no DSR value
3052:    * the card default value (0x0404) will be used.
3053:    */
3054: 
3055:   mmcsd_sendcmd4(priv);
3056: 
3057:   /* Select the card.
3058:    * Send CMD7 with the argument == RCA in order to select the card
3059:    * and send it in data-trasfer mode. Since we are supporting
3060:    * only a single card, we just leave the card selected all of the time.
3061:    */
3062: 
3063:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD7S, (uint32_t)priv->rca << 16);
3064:   ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD7S);
3065:   if (ret != OK)
3066:     {
3067:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_recv_r1 for CMD7 failed: %d\n", ret);
3068:       return ret;
3069:     }
3070: 
3071:   /* If the hardware only supports 4-bit transfer mode then we forced to
3072:    * attempt to setup the card in this mode before checking the ext CSD
3073:    * register.
3074:    */
3075: 
3076:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_4BIT_ONLY) != 0)
3077:     {
3078:       /* Select width (4-bit) bus operation */
3079: 
3080:       priv->buswidth = MMCSD_SCR_BUSWIDTH_4BIT;
3081:       ret = mmcsd_widebus(priv);
3082: 
3083:       if (ret != OK)
3084:         {
3085:           ferr("ERROR: Failed to set wide bus operation: %d\n", ret);
3086:         }
3087:     }
3088: 
3089:   /* CSD Decoding for MMC should be done after entering in data-transfer mode
3090:    * because if the card has block addressing then extended CSD register
3091:    * must be read in order to get the right number of blocks and capacity,
3092:    * and BUS width but it has to be done in data-transfer mode.
3093:    */
3094: 
3095:   if (IS_BLOCK(priv->type))
3096:     {
3097:       finfo("Card supports eMMC spec 4.0 (or greater). Reading ext_csd.\n");
3098:       ret = mmcsd_read_extcsd(priv, extcsd);
3099:       if (ret != OK)
3100:         {
3101:           ferr("ERROR: Failed to determinate number of blocks: %d\n", ret);
3102:           return ret;
3103:         }
3104: 
3105:       mmcsd_decode_extcsd(priv, extcsd);
3106:     }
3107: 
3108:   mmcsd_decode_csd(priv, priv->csd);
3109: 
3110:   /* It's up to the driver to act on the widebus request.  mmcsd_widebus()
3111:    * enables the CLOCK_MMC_TRANSFER, so call it here always.
3112:    */
3113: 
3114:   ret = mmcsd_widebus(priv);
3115:   if (ret != OK)
3116:     {
3117:       ferr("ERROR: Failed to set wide bus operation: %d\n", ret);
3118:     }
3119: 
3120:   return OK;
3121: }

3123: /****************************************************************************
3124:  * Name: mmcsd_read_extcsd
3125:  *
3126:  * Description:
3127:  *   MMC card is detected with block addressing and this function will read
3128:  *   the correct number of blocks and capacity. Returns OK if ext CSD is read
3129:  *   correctly or error in not.
3130:  *
3131:  *   Note:  For some MCU architectures, buffer[] must be aligned.
3132:  *
3133:  ****************************************************************************/
3134: 
3135: static int mmcsd_read_extcsd(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv,
3136:                              FAR uint8_t *extcsd)
3137: {
3138:   int ret;
3139: 
3140:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL);
3141: 
3142:   /* Check if the card is locked */
3143: 
3144:   if (priv->locked)
3145:     {
3146:       ferr("ERROR: Card is locked\n");
3147:       return -EPERM;
3148:     }
3149: 
3150:   memset(extcsd, 0, 512);
3151: 
3152: #if defined(CONFIG_SDIO_DMA) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_SDIO_PREFLIGHT)
3153: 
3154:   /* If we think we are going to perform a DMA transfer, make sure that we
3155:    * will be able to before we commit the card to the operation.
3156:    */
3157: 
3158:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
3159:     {
3160:       ret = SDIO_DMAPREFLIGHT(priv->dev, extcsd, priv->blocksize);
3161:       if (ret != OK)
3162:         {
3163:           return ret;
3164:         }
3165:     }
3166: #endif
3167: 
3168:   /* Verify that the card is ready for the transfer.  The card may still be
3169:    * busy from the preceding write transfer.  It would be simpler to check
3170:    * for write busy at the end of each write, rather than at the beginning of
3171:    * each read AND write, but putting the busy-wait at the beginning of the
3172:    * transfer allows for more overlap and, hopefully, better performance
3173:    */
3174: 
3175:   ret = mmcsd_transferready(priv);
3176:   if (ret != OK)
3177:     {
3178:       ferr("ERROR: Card not ready: %d\n", ret);
3179:       return ret;
3180:     }
3181: 
3182:   /* Select the block size for the card (CMD16) */
3183: 
3184:   ret = mmcsd_setblocklen(priv, 512);
3185:   if (ret != OK)
3186:     {
3187:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_setblocklen failed: %d\n", ret);
3188:       return ret;
3189:     }
3190: 
3191:   /* Configure SDIO controller hardware for the read transfer */
3192: 
3193:   SDIO_BLOCKSETUP(priv->dev, 512, 1);
3194:   SDIO_WAITENABLE(priv->dev,
3195:                   SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR,
3196:                   MMCSD_BLOCK_RDATADELAY);
3197: 
3198: #ifdef CONFIG_SDIO_DMA
3199:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
3200:     {
3201:       finfo("Setting up for DMA transfer.\n");
3202:       ret = SDIO_DMARECVSETUP(priv->dev, extcsd, 512);
3203:       if (ret != OK)
3204:         {
3205:           ferr("SDIO_DMARECVSETUP: error %d\n", ret);
3206:           SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
3207:           return ret;
3208:         }
3209:     }
3210:   else
3211: #endif
3212:     {
3213:       SDIO_RECVSETUP(priv->dev, extcsd, 512);
3214:     }
3215: 
3216:   /* Send CMD8 in data-transfer mode to obtain the
3217:    * extended Card Specific Data (CSD) register, e.g., block length, card
3218:    * storage capacity, etc.
3219:    */
3220: 
3221:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMC_CMD8, 0);
3222:   ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMC_CMD8);
3223:   if (ret != OK)
3224:     {
3225:       ferr("ERROR: Could not get MMC extended CSD register: %d\n", ret);
3226:       SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
3227:       return ret;
3228:     }
3229: 
3230:   /* Then wait for the data transfer to complete */
3231: 
3232:   ret = mmcsd_eventwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
3233:   if (ret != OK)
3234:     {
3235:       ferr("ERROR: CMD17 transfer failed: %d\n", ret);
3236:       return ret;
3237:     }
3238: 
3239:   SDIO_GOTEXTCSD(priv->dev, extcsd);
3240: 
3241:   /* Return value:  One sector read */
3242: 
3243:   return OK;
3244: }
3245: #endif

3247: #ifdef CONFIG_MMCSD_IOCSUPPORT
3248: /****************************************************************************
3249:  * Name: mmcsd_general_cmd_write
3250:  *
3251:  * Description:
3252:  *   Send cmd56 data, one sector size
3253:  *
3254:  ****************************************************************************/
3255: 
3256: static int mmcsd_general_cmd_write(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv,
3257:                                    FAR const uint8_t *buffer,
3258:                                    off_t startblock)
3259: {
3260:   int ret;
3261: 
3262:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && buffer != NULL);
3263: 
3264:   /* Check if the card is locked or write protected (either via software or
3265:    * via the mechanical write protect on the card)
3266:    */
3267: 
3268:   if (mmcsd_wrprotected(priv))
3269:     {
3270:       ferr("ERROR: Card is locked or write protected\n");
3271:       return -EPERM;
3272:     }
3273: 
3274: #if defined(CONFIG_SDIO_DMA) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_SDIO_PREFLIGHT)
3275:   /* If we think we are going to perform a DMA transfer, make sure that we
3276:    * will be able to before we commit the card to the operation.
3277:    */
3278: 
3279:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
3280:     {
3281:       ret = SDIO_DMAPREFLIGHT(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
3282:       if (ret != OK)
3283:         {
3284:           return ret;
3285:         }
3286:     }
3287: #endif
3288: 
3289:   /* Verify that the card is ready for the transfer.  The card may still be
3290:    * busy from the preceding write transfer.  It would be simpler to check
3291:    * for write busy at the end of each write, rather than at the beginning of
3292:    * each read AND write, but putting the busy-wait at the beginning of the
3293:    * transfer allows for more overlap and, hopefully, better performance
3294:    */
3295: 
3296:   ret = mmcsd_transferready(priv);
3297:   if (ret != OK)
3298:     {
3299:       ferr("ERROR: Card not ready: %d\n", ret);
3300:       return ret;
3301:     }
3302: 
3303:   /* Select the block size for the card */
3304: 
3305:   ret = mmcsd_setblocklen(priv, priv->blocksize);
3306:   if (ret != OK)
3307:     {
3308:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_setblocklen failed: %d\n", ret);
3309:       return ret;
3310:     }
3311: 
3312:   /* If Controller does not need DMA setup before the write then send CMD56
3313:    * now.
3314:    */
3315: 
3316:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMABEFOREWRITE) == 0)
3317:     {
3318:       /* Send CMD56, WRITE_BLOCK, and verify good R1 status is returned */
3319: 
3320:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD56WR, startblock);
3321:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD56WR);
3322:       if (ret != OK)
3323:         {
3324:           ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_recv_r1 for CMD56 failed: %d\n", ret);
3325:           return ret;
3326:         }
3327:     }
3328: 
3329:   /* Configure SDIO controller hardware for the write transfer */
3330: 
3331:   SDIO_BLOCKSETUP(priv->dev, priv->blocksize, 1);
3332:   SDIO_WAITENABLE(priv->dev,
3333:                   SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR,
3334:                   MMCSD_BLOCK_WDATADELAY);
3335: 
3336: #ifdef CONFIG_SDIO_DMA
3337:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
3338:     {
3339:       ret = SDIO_DMASENDSETUP(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
3340:       if (ret != OK)
3341:         {
3342:           finfo("SDIO_DMASENDSETUP: error %d\n", ret);
3343:           SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
3344:           return ret;
3345:         }
3346:     }
3347:   else
3348: #endif
3349:     {
3350:       SDIO_SENDSETUP(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
3351:     }
3352: 
3353:   /* If Controller needs DMA setup before write then only send CMD24 now. */
3354: 
3355:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMABEFOREWRITE) != 0)
3356:     {
3357:       /* Send CMD56, WRITE_BLOCK, and verify good R1 status is returned */
3358: 
3359:       mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD56WR, startblock);
3360:       ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD56WR);
3361:       if (ret != OK)
3362:         {
3363:           ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_recv_r1 for CMD56 failed: %d\n", ret);
3364:           SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
3365:           return ret;
3366:         }
3367:     }
3368: 
3369:   /* Wait for the transfer to complete */
3370: 
3371:   ret = mmcsd_eventwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);
3372:   if (ret != OK)
3373:     {
3374:       ferr("ERROR: CMD56 transfer failed: %d\n", ret);
3375:       return ret;
3376:     }
3377: 
3378:   /* Flag that a write transfer is pending that we will have to check for
3379:    * write complete at the beginning of the next transfer.
3380:    */
3381: 
3382:   priv->wrbusy = true;
3383: 
3384: #if defined(CONFIG_MMCSD_SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE)
3385:   /* Arm the write complete detection with timeout */
3386: 
3387:   SDIO_WAITENABLE(priv->dev, SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT,
3388:                   MMCSD_BLOCK_WDATADELAY);
3389: #endif
3390: 
3391:   /* On success, return OK */
3392: 
3393:   return OK;
3394: }

3396: /****************************************************************************
3397:  * Name: mmcsd_general_cmd_read
3398:  *
3399:  * Description:
3400:  *   Read cmd56 data, one sector size
3401:  *
3402:  ****************************************************************************/
3403: 
3404: static int mmcsd_general_cmd_read(FAR struct mmcsd_state_s *priv,
3405:                                   FAR uint8_t *buffer, off_t startblock)
3406: {
3407:   int ret;
3408: 
3409:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && buffer != NULL);
3410: 
3411:   /* Check if the card is locked */
3412: 
3413:   if (priv->locked)
3414:     {
3415:       ferr("ERROR: Card is locked\n");
3416:       return -EPERM;
3417:     }
3418: 
3419: #if defined(CONFIG_SDIO_DMA) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_SDIO_PREFLIGHT)
3420:   /* If we think we are going to perform a DMA transfer, make sure that we
3421:    * will be able to before we commit the card to the operation.
3422:    */
3423: 
3424:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
3425:     {
3426:       ret = SDIO_DMAPREFLIGHT(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
3427:       if (ret != OK)
3428:         {
3429:           return ret;
3430:         }
3431:     }
3432: #endif
3433: 
3434:   /* Verify that the card is ready for the transfer.  The card may still be
3435:    * busy from the preceding write transfer.  It would be simpler to check
3436:    * for write busy at the end of each write, rather than at the beginning of
3437:    * each read AND write, but putting the busy-wait at the beginning of the
3438:    * transfer allows for more overlap and, hopefully, better performance
3439:    */
3440: 
3441:   ret = mmcsd_transferready(priv);
3442:   if (ret != OK)
3443:     {
3444:       ferr("ERROR: Card not ready: %d\n", ret);
3445:       return ret;
3446:     }
3447: 
3448:   /* Select the block size for the card */
3449: 
3450:   ret = mmcsd_setblocklen(priv, priv->blocksize);
3451:   if (ret != OK)
3452:     {
3453:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_setblocklen failed: %d\n", ret);
3454:       return ret;
3455:     }
3456: 
3457:   /* Configure SDIO controller hardware for the read transfer */
3458: 
3459:   SDIO_BLOCKSETUP(priv->dev, priv->blocksize, 1);
3460:   SDIO_WAITENABLE(priv->dev,
3461:                   SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR,
3462:                   MMCSD_BLOCK_RDATADELAY);
3463: 
3464: #ifdef CONFIG_SDIO_DMA
3465:   if ((priv->caps & SDIO_CAPS_DMASUPPORTED) != 0)
3466:     {
3467:       ret = SDIO_DMARECVSETUP(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
3468:       if (ret != OK)
3469:         {
3470:           finfo("SDIO_DMARECVSETUP: error %d\n", ret);
3471:           SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
3472:           return ret;
3473:         }
3474:     }
3475:   else
3476: #endif
3477:     {
3478:       SDIO_RECVSETUP(priv->dev, buffer, priv->blocksize);
3479:     }
3480: 
3481:   /* Send CMD56: Read a sector size data and verify that good R1
3482:    * status is returned.
3483:    */
3484: 
3485:   mmcsd_sendcmdpoll(priv, MMCSD_CMD56RD, startblock);
3486:   ret = mmcsd_recv_r1(priv, MMCSD_CMD56RD);
3487:   if (ret != OK)
3488:     {
3489:       ferr("ERROR: mmcsd_recv_r1 for CMD56 failed: %d\n", ret);
3490:       SDIO_CANCEL(priv->dev);
3491:       return ret;
3492:     }
3493: 
3494:   /* Then wait for the data transfer to complete */
3495: 
3496:   ret = mmcsd_eventwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT | SDIOWAIT_ERROR);

2502: /****************************************************************************
2503:  * Name: stm32_eventwait
2504:  *
2505:  * Description:
2506:  *   Wait for one of the enabled events to occur (or a timeout).  Note that
2507:  *   all events enabled by SDIO_WAITEVENTS are disabled when stm32_eventwait
2508:  *   returns.  SDIO_WAITEVENTS must be called again before stm32_eventwait
2509:  *   can be used again.
2510:  *
2511:  * Input Parameters:
2512:  *   dev     - An instance of the SDIO device interface
2513:  *   timeout - Maximum time in milliseconds to wait.  Zero means immediate
2514:  *             timeout with no wait.  The timeout value is ignored if
2515:  *             SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT is not included in the waited-for eventset.
2516:  *
2517:  * Returned Value:
2518:  *   Event set containing the event(s) that ended the wait.  Should always
2519:  *   be non-zero.  All events are disabled after the wait concludes.
2520:  *
2521:  ****************************************************************************/
2522: 
2523: static sdio_eventset_t stm32_eventwait(struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
2524: {
2525:   struct stm32_dev_s *priv = (struct stm32_dev_s *)dev;
2526:   sdio_eventset_t wkupevent = 0;
2527:   irqstate_t flags;
2528:   int ret;
2529: 
2530:   /* There is a race condition here... the event may have completed before
2531:    * we get here.  In this case waitevents will be zero, but wkupevents will
2532:    * be non-zero (and, hopefully, the semaphore count will also be non-zero.
2533:    */
2534: 
2535:   flags = enter_critical_section();
2536: 
2537: #if defined(CONFIG_MMCSD_SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE)
2538:   /* A card ejected while in SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE can lead to a
2539:    * condition where there is no waitevents set and no wkupevent
2540:    */
2541: 
2542:   if (priv->waitevents == 0 && priv->wkupevent == 0)
2543:     {
2544:       wkupevent = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
2545:       goto errout_with_waitints;
2546:     }
2547: 
2548: #else
2549:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->waitevents != 0 || priv->wkupevent != 0);
2550: #endif
2551: 
2552: #if defined(CONFIG_MMCSD_SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE)
2553:   if ((priv->waitevents & SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE) != 0)
2554:     {
2555:       /* Atomically read pin to see if ready (true) and determine if ISR
2556:        * fired.  If Pin is ready and if ISR did NOT fire end the wait here.
2557:        */
2558: 
2559:       if (stm32_gpioread(GPIO_SDIO_D0) &&
2560:          (priv->wkupevent & SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE) == 0)
2561:         {
2562:           stm32_endwait(priv, SDIOWAIT_WRCOMPLETE);
2563:         }
2564:     }
2565: #endif
2566: 
2567:   /* Loop until the event (or the timeout occurs). Race conditions are
2568:    * avoided by calling stm32_waitenable prior to triggering the logic that
2569:    * will cause the wait to terminate.  Under certain race conditions, the
2570:    * waited-for may have already occurred before this function was called!
2571:    */
2572: 
2573:   for (; ; )
2574:     {
2575:       /* Wait for an event in event set to occur.  If this the event has
2576:        * already occurred, then the semaphore will already have been
2577:        * incremented and there will be no wait.
2578:        */
2579: 
2580:       ret = nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&priv->waitsem);
2581:       if (ret < 0)
2582:         {
2583:           /* Task canceled.  Cancel the wdog (assuming it was started) and
2584:            * return an SDIO error.
2585:            */
2586: 
2587:           wd_cancel(&priv->waitwdog);
2588:           wkupevent = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
2589:           goto errout_with_waitints;
2590:         }
2591: 
2592:       wkupevent = priv->wkupevent;
2593: 
2594:       /* Check if the event has occurred.  When the event has occurred, then
2595:        * evenset will be set to 0 and wkupevent will be set to a nonzero
2596:        * value.
2597:        */
2598: 
2599:       if (wkupevent != 0)
2600:         {
2601:           /* Yes... break out of the loop with wkupevent non-zero */
2602: 
2603:           break;
2604:         }
2605:     }
2606: 
2607:   /* Disable event-related interrupts */
2608: 
2609: errout_with_waitints:
2610:   stm32_configwaitints(priv, 0, 0, 0);
2611: #ifdef CONFIG_STM32_SDIO_DMA
2612:   priv->xfrflags   = 0;
2613: #endif
2614: 
2615:   leave_critical_section(flags);
2616:   stm32_dumpsamples(priv);
2617:   return wkupevent;
2618: }

2692: /****************************************************************************
2693:  * Name: stm32_dmapreflight
2694:  *
2695:  * Description:

1727:       regval |= SDMMC_CMD_SHORTRESPONSE;
1728:       break;
1729: 
1730:     case MMCSD_R3_RESPONSE:
1731:     case MMCSD_R4_RESPONSE:

1734: 
1735:     case MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE:
1736:     case MMCSD_R5_RESPONSE:
1737:     case MMCSD_R6_RESPONSE:
1738:     case MMCSD_R7_RESPONSE:

1951:    */

1973: /****************************************************************************
1974:  * Name: esp32s3_waitresponse
1975:  *
1976:  * Description:
1977:  *   Poll-wait for the response to the last command to be ready.
1978:  *
1979:  * Input Parameters:
1980:  *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
1981:  *   cmd  - The command that was sent.  See 32-bit command definitions above.
1982:  *
1983:  * Returned Value:
1984:  *   OK is success; a negated errno on failure
1985:  *
1986:  ****************************************************************************/
1987: 
1988: static int esp32s3_waitresponse(struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd)
1989: {
1990:   int ret = OK;
1991:   volatile int32_t timeout;
1992:   clock_t watchtime;
1993: 
1994:   mcinfo("cmd=%04x\n", cmd);
1995: 
1996:   switch (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK)
1997:     {
1998:     case MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE:
1999:     case MMCSD_R3_RESPONSE:
2000:     case MMCSD_R7_RESPONSE:
2001:       timeout = SDCARD_CMDTIMEOUT;
2002:       break;
2003: 
2004:     case MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE:
2005:     case MMCSD_R1B_RESPONSE:
2006:     case MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE:
2007:     case MMCSD_R4_RESPONSE:
2008:     case MMCSD_R5_RESPONSE:
2009:     case MMCSD_R6_RESPONSE:
2010:       timeout = SDCARD_LONGTIMEOUT;
2011:       break;
2012: 
2013:     default:
2014:       return -EINVAL;
2015:     }
2016: 
2017:   watchtime = clock_systime_ticks();
2018: 
2019:   /* We should wait for CMDDONE, even if there is a response error. */
2020: 
2021:   while ((esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS) & SDMMC_INT_CDONE) == 0)
2022:     {
2023:       if (clock_systime_ticks() - watchtime > timeout)
2024:         {
2025:           mcerr("ERROR: Timeout cmd: %04x STA: %08x RINTSTS: %08x\n",
2026:                 cmd, esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS),
2027:                 esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS));
2028: 
2029:           ret = -ETIMEDOUT;
2030:         }
2031:     }
2032: 
2033:   /* Check if there is a response error. */
2034: 
2035:   if (esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS) & SDCARD_INT_RESPERR)
2036:     {
2037:       mcerr("ERROR: SDMMC failure cmd: %04x STA: %08x RINTSTS: %08x\n",
2038:             cmd, esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_STATUS),
2039:             esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS));
2040:       ret = -EIO;
2041:     }
2042: 
2043:   esp32s3_putreg(SDCARD_CMDDONE_CLEAR, ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
2044:   return ret;
2045: }
