2047: /****************************************************************************
2048:  * Name: esp32s3_recvshortcrc
2049:  *
2050:  * Description:
2051:  *   Receive response to SDIO command.  Only the critical payload is
2052:  *   returned -- 32 bits for 48 bit status.  The driver implementation
2053:  *   verifies the correctness of the remaining, non-returned bits (CRCs, CMD
2054:  *   index, etc.).
2055:  *
2056:  * Input Parameters:
2057:  *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
2058:  *   Rx   - Buffer in which to receive the response
2059:  *
2060:  * Returned Value:
2061:  *   Number of bytes sent on success; a negated errno on failure.  Here a
2062:  *   failure means only a faiure to obtain the requested response (due to
2063:  *   transport problem -- timeout, CRC, etc.).  The implementation only
2064:  *   assures that the response is returned intacta and does not check errors
2065:  *   within the response itself.
2066:  *
2067:  ****************************************************************************/
2068: 
2069: static int esp32s3_recvshortcrc(struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd,
2070:                                 uint32_t *rshort)
2071: {
2072:   uint32_t regval;
2073:   int ret = OK;
2074: 
2075:   mcinfo("cmd=%04x\n", cmd);
2076: 
2077:   /* R1  Command response (48-bit)
2078:    *     47        0               Start bit
2079:    *     46        0               Transmission bit (0=from card)
2080:    *     45:40     bit5   - bit0   Command index (0-63)
2081:    *     39:8      bit31  - bit0   32-bit card status
2082:    *     7:1       bit6   - bit0   CRC7
2083:    *     0         1               End bit
2084:    *
2085:    * R1b Identical to R1 with the additional busy signaling via the data
2086:    *     line.
2087:    *
2088:    * R6  Published RCA Response (48-bit, SD card only)
2089:    *     47        0               Start bit
2090:    *     46        0               Transmission bit (0=from card)
2091:    *     45:40     bit5   - bit0   Command index (0-63)
2092:    *     39:8      bit31  - bit0   32-bit Argument Field, consisting of:
2093:    *                               [31:16] New published RCA of card
2094:    *                               [15:0]  Card status bits {23,22,19,12:0}
2095:    *     7:1       bit6   - bit0   CRC7
2096:    *     0         1               End bit
2097:    */
2098: 
2099: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
2100:   if (!rshort)
2101:     {
2102:       mcerr("ERROR: rshort=NULL\n");
2103:       ret = -EINVAL;
2104:     }
2105: 
2106:   /* Check that this is the correct response to this command */
2107: 
2108:   else if ((cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) != MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE &&
2109:            (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) != MMCSD_R1B_RESPONSE &&
2110:            (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) != MMCSD_R6_RESPONSE)
2111:     {
2112:       mcerr("ERROR: Wrong response CMD=%04x\n", cmd);
2113:       ret = -EINVAL;
2114:     }
2115:   else
2116: #endif
2117:     {
2118:       /* Check if a timeout or CRC error occurred */
2119: 
2120:       regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
2121:       if ((regval & SDMMC_INT_RTO) != 0)
2122:         {
2123:           mcerr("ERROR: Command timeout: %08x\n", regval);
2124:           ret = -ETIMEDOUT;
2125:         }
2126:       else if ((regval & SDMMC_INT_RCRC) != 0)
2127:         {
2128:           mcerr("ERROR: CRC failure: %08x\n", regval);
2129:           ret = -EIO;
2130:         }
2131:     }
2132: 
2133:   /* Clear all pending message completion events and return the R1/R6
2134:    * response.
2135:    */
2136: 
2137:   esp32s3_putreg(SDCARD_RESPDONE_CLEAR | SDCARD_CMDDONE_CLEAR,
2138:                  ESP32S3_SDMMC_RINTSTS);
2139:   *rshort = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_SDMMC_RESP0);
2140:   mcinfo("CRC=%04x\n", *rshort);
2141: 
2142:   return ret;
2143: }

text:
**Scope And Configuration**

The active board configuration is SD-only, 1-bit PIO, block setup enabled, DMA disabled, one block per transfer, and read-only:

- `CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1`
- `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY=y`
- `CONFIG_SDIO_BLOCKSETUP=y`
- `CONFIG_SDIO_DMA` disabled
- MMC support and card detect disabled

See [defconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:80).

**Exact Upper-Half Behavior**

Initialization starts in `mmcsd_slotinitialize()` and proceeds through `mmcsd_hwinitialize()`:

1. Read lower-half capabilities.
2. Call `SDIO_ATTACH()`.
3. Call `SDIO_REGISTERCALLBACK()`; its return value is ignored.
4. Read `SDIO_STATUS()`.
5. Probe and initialize the card.

References: [mmcsd_slotinitialize()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:4561), [mmcsd_hwinitialize()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:4440), and the API contracts in [sdio.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/sdio.h:547).

With MMC support disabled, SD identification is:

`CLOCK_IDMODE` → CMD0 twice → CMD8/R7 → repeated CMD55/R1 + ACMD41/R3 → CMD2/R2 → CMD3/R6 → CMD13/R1 → CMD9/R2 → CMD7/R1b → transfer clock → SCR.

Every command is issued as:

`SDIO_SENDCMD()` → `SDIO_WAITRESPONSE()` → a separate `SDIO_RECVR*()` call.

`mmcsd_sendcmdpoll()` performs only the first two operations; card-level response decoding is done afterward. See [mmcsd_sendcmdpoll()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:329). R1 errors are interpreted by the upper half, while lower-half response methods are responsible only for transport integrity.

For ACMD51/SCR, the exact order is unusual:

`CMD16(8)` → `BLOCKSETUP(8,1)` → `RECVSETUP(scr,8)` → `WAITENABLE(TRANSFERDONE|TIMEOUT|ERROR,100ms)` → CMD55/wait/R1 → ACMD51/wait/R1 → `EVENTWAIT()`.

See [mmcsd_get_scr()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:493). This places `RECVSETUP` before `WAITENABLE`, unlike the recommended race-free ordering in [sdio.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/sdio.h:718). No data command has been sent yet, so a polling lower half can support it, but `waitenable()` must not invalidate the prepared transfer.

For ordinary reads with `MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1`, `mmcsd_read()` loops over sectors and calls `mmcsd_readsingle()` once per sector. Each sector uses:

`CMD16(512)` if needed → `BLOCKSETUP(512,1)` → `WAITENABLE(...,100ms)` → `RECVSETUP(buffer,512)` → CMD17/wait/R1 → `EVENTWAIT()`.

See [mmcsd_readsingle()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:1484) and [mmcsd_read()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:2335). CMD18, CMD23, CMD12, and all upper-half multi-block helpers are compiled out when the limit is exactly one.

For writes, the declared lower-half capability does not request “DMA before write”, so the upper half would issue CMD24 and receive R1 before calling `BLOCKSETUP`, `WAITENABLE`, and `SENDSETUP`. That ordering matches the PIO `SENDSETUP` description in [sdio.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/sdio.h:628).

**Lower-Half Contract Violations**

1. **R2 commands are never configured as long-response commands.**

   In [sdio_sendcmd()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:171), `response` is shifted down to `0..8`, but it is compared with `MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE`, whose value remains shifted (`3 << 6`, or `0xc0`). Thus `3 == 0xc0` is always false. CMD2 and CMD9 are sent without the lower half’s long-response selection, while [sdio_recv_r2()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:214) subsequently reads four words.

   Fix: compare `(cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) == MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE`, or compare the shifted value to `MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE >> MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT`.

2. **A 512-byte single-block transfer is incorrectly marked multiblock.**

   [sdio_recvsetup()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:320) selects `BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK` whenever `blocklen == 512`. The upper half explicitly calls `BLOCKSETUP(512,1)` followed by CMD17, so this condition configures every normal single-sector read as multiblock.

   Fix: derive multiblock state from `nblocks > 1`, not block length. With the current configuration it should never be selected by the MMCSD upper half.

3. **Response transport failures are lost before `RECVR*`.**

   [sdio_wait_command()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:105) clears command timeout and CRC status before returning. Every `sdio_recv_r*()` then reads response registers and returns `OK` unconditionally. No command identity, requested response type, timeout, or CRC state is validated there.

   This is particularly dangerous because the upper half ignores many `mmcsd_sendcmdpoll()` return values, including CMD55/ACMD51 and CMD17. A failed `WAITRESPONSE` can therefore be followed by a successful-looking stale `RECVR1`.

   Fix: retain the last command and transport result in `priv`, and have each `recv_r*()` validate and return that result. Alternatively, leave response status intact until `recv_r*()` validates and clears it. Validate the requested response type and command identity where the interface permits.

4. **CRC policy is based on command index and suppresses required R2 checks.**

   CRC checking is disabled for CMD2 and CMD9 in both `sdio_sendcmd()` and `sdio_wait_command()`. R2 carries a CRC and the SDIO contract requires response integrity verification. ACMD41/R3 legitimately has no response CRC; CMD2/CMD9 do not belong in the same category.

   Fix: derive CRC behavior from `cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK`: omit CRC only for no-response, R3, and R4 responses; require it for R1/R1b/R2/R5/R6/R7.

5. **`waitenable()` and `eventwait()` do not implement the documented event contract.**

   [sdio_waitenable()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:389) maps timeout zero to 1000 ms, although zero means immediate timeout. `eventwait()` applies a deadline even if `SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT` was not enabled, does not mask results against `wait_events`, and does not support CMDDONE or RESPONSEDONE events. It clears only the software event set on return, while the receive-event mask enabled by `recvsetup()` remains enabled.

   Fix: preserve zero as immediate timeout; ignore the timeout argument unless `SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT` is selected; recognize only enabled events; disable all wait-related sources before returning; and preserve an already-recorded event so `EVENTWAIT` can observe completion that occurred before it was called.

6. **`waitenable()` does not discard pending wait events as required.**

   The contract requires it to discard pending events before arming the new set. The current function only updates fields. `recvsetup()` happens to clear status, but SCR and CMD17 use different `WAITENABLE`/`RECVSETUP` orderings, so correctness currently depends on the caller’s setup sequence.

   Fix: centralize stale-event clearing in `waitenable()`, while ensuring it clears old completion state without canceling the transfer prepared by SCR’s earlier `recvsetup()`.

7. **PIO receive servicing is deferred until receive-end or error.**

   [sdio_eventwait()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:550) does not drain data while a transfer is active; it drains only after receive-end or in one error path. It ignores the available-data indication during the active polling loop. A PIO `RECVSETUP` implementation must move data as necessary to complete the requested transfer, not merely wait for the final event.

   Fix: service available receive data continuously while polling, then treat receive-end as successful only when exactly `nbytes` has been copied.

8. **Callback registration falsely succeeds without registering anything.**

   [sdio_registercallback()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:653) discards the callback and argument and returns `OK`; `callbackenable()` is also a no-op. This violates the one-shot callback semantics in [sdio.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/sdio.h:778).

   It is dormant after a successful probe because card detect is disabled, but it matters after an initial probe failure when the upper half enables `SDIOMEDIA_INSERTED`.

   Fix: store callback, argument, and enabled event mask; registration must disable events; callback delivery must clear the mask. For immutable fixed media, storing the registration without generating transitions is sufficient.

9. **Controller lifecycle state is incomplete.**

   `sdio_clock()` ignores `CLOCK_SDIO_DISABLED`; `sdio_reset()` leaves block size/count, buffer, wait events, and timeout state intact; `cancel()` does not disable wait-event sources or clear all transfer state. These conflict with the reset, clock, cancel, and post-`EVENTWAIT` cleanup contracts.

   Fix: implement disabled clock state and comprehensively clear transfer/wait state on reset, cancel, and completed waits. Guard `blocksetup` and its vtable initializer with `CONFIG_SDIO_BLOCKSETUP` so the lower half also builds when that option is disabled.

**Read-Only Defect In The Upper Half**

`CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY` is not honored by `mmcsd_sdio.c`. It still installs `mmcsd_write`, registers block devices with mode `0666`, reports write-enabled geometry when card status allows it, and retains CMD24/CMD56 write paths. Compare [g_bops](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:239) and registration at [mmcsd_probe()](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:4346) with the correctly guarded SPI implementation at [mmcsd_spi.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_spi.c:62).

The BK lower half returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` from `sendsetup()`, but the upper half ignores non-DMA `SENDSETUP` return values. A write can therefore send CMD24 first and only fail later by timeout.

The proper fix is in `mmcsd_sdio.c`: set mode `0444`, install a `NULL` write operation, report `geo_writeenabled=false`, compile out or reject write helpers and write ioctls with `-EROFS`, and check all PIO setup return values. As a defensive lower-half measure, this fixed read-only port can report `SDIO_STATUS_WRPROTECTED` when `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY` is enabled.

**Actual Board Read Path**

The exposed `/dev/mmcsd0` does not use the upper-half CMD17 path. [bk7258_mmcsd_initialize()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:115) always unregisters the MMCSD block driver and installs its fallback, even when `mmcsd_slotinitialize()` succeeds.

That fallback calls [bk7258_sdio_read_blocks()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:427), which accepts only one block but sends CMD18 and CMD12. This contradicts `MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1` and bypasses the upper-half single-block behavior.

Concrete fix: retain the upper-half block device when initialization succeeds. If the fallback remains necessary, change its one-block transaction to CMD17 and remove CMD12; also avoid hardcoding byte addressing independently of the card type discovered during initialization. No files were modified.
